comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**The intended design, settled: a config file per daemon, written by
Muster when it starts one, and handed to that daemon alone.** Muster
owns `scrollback` (and whatever follows) in `~/.muster/config.toml`,
translates it, and the user never learns which daemon read what.

That is the same move already made for the renderer, so the half that is
ours needs no permission and is small: `~/.muster/state/libghostty.conf`
is written every launch from what the config file said, and a derived
herdr config beside it works the same way - derived, not editable, and
worth reading because it answers what Muster actually told the daemon.

**Confirmed there is no way to do it today**, checked rather than assumed
while settling this: v0.8.0 is the newest herdr tag, `config_dir()` reads
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` and nothing else, `herdr server` has no
`--config`, and the only `HERDR_*` variables herdr reads anywhere are
debug, test and Windows-input ones. There is no path to hand a daemon a
config without handing its panes the same directory.

**One workaround was considered and rejected**, so nobody spends an
afternoon rediscovering it: point the daemon's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` at a
Muster-private directory holding its own `herdr/` plus a symlink to every
other entry of the real `~/.config`. Reads and writes to directories that
already exist pass straight through, so it very nearly works. It fails on
*new* top-level entries - a program that creates `~/.config/something`
creates it inside Muster's private directory, where nothing else will
ever look for it. Muster could sweep strays back on the next launch, but
then Muster is repairing somebody's config directory, which is well
outside its business and an excellent way to lose their data. A pane runs
arbitrary programs; this is not a risk to take for a scrollback setting.

**A wrinkle to design for rather than discover: the config has to land
where the daemon can read it.** A window can be attached to a daemon on
another machine, so "write it on the fly" is trivial locally and a file
that has to reach the far side over the existing ssh master for a devenv.
Per-daemon is right for a second reason too - two machines can want
different answers, and a single Muster-wide daemon config would have to
pretend otherwise.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A person who wants deeper scrollback has to learn that herdr exists, find
its config file, and edit it. The desideratum now says that is wrong -
"where Muster acts on the answer, the way to ask is Muster's, never the
dependency's" - and this is the card that makes it true of the config
file rather than only of the README.

**Blocked on a_28adIUgPE**, and only on that.

**It is an inconsistency, not a boundary.** The config rule already
reads: a setting is Muster's when Muster acts on the answer, *including
the ones it only translates onward for libghostty*. Muster does not
consume `[font]` or `[colors]` either - it writes a derived
`libghostty.conf` and hands it over. Translating onward to the daemon is
the same move. It has simply never had a mechanism, and the absence of a
mechanism turned into a rule in the docs.

Three candidates, in increasing order of how much they matter:

1. **Scrollback depth.** The motivating case, and purely ergonomic: it is
   obviously a user setting, and today it is somewhere else.
2. **What a pane runs** (`default_shell`, `shell_mode`). Muster decides
   what a pane *is*; a `default_shell` somebody set for their own
   terminal silently deciding what every Muster pane runs is the surprise
   a_28adIUgPE already describes.
3. **Update checks.** `version_check` and `manifest_check` default to
   **true** in herdr, so Muster's bundled daemon - pinned by version and
   checksum, downloaded and verified by `./dev`, shipped inside the app -
   is checking for its own updates against a config file Muster does not
   own and cannot read the intent of. This one is not ergonomics. Pinning
   the daemon is what makes "green suite means it works" mean anything,
   and right now nothing stops the pinned daemon being told to move off
   the pin by a file Muster never sees.

The blocker, verified again against 0.8.0 while writing this: herdr
resolves its config directory from `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, panes inherit the
daemon's environment, and so a private config directory for the daemon is
a private config directory for every pane's git, editor and shell.
`config_dir()` reads `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` and nothing else, and
`herdr server` has no `--config` flag.

**When it lands, the shape is already prototyped.** Muster writes
`~/.muster/state/libghostty.conf` every launch: derived, not editable,
and worth reading precisely because it answers "what did Muster actually
tell the renderer". A `herdr.toml` beside it, on the same terms, gives
the same answer for the daemon - and the first question when a pane opens
the wrong shell becomes a file you can read rather than a guess about
whose config won.

Two things to decide when writing it, rather than discover:

- **Which of the three are settings at all.** Update checks are not a
  user's choice in a bundled daemon - they are a thing Muster should turn
  off and not offer, the way it does not offer to change which herdr it
  runs. Scrollback plainly is a user's. What a pane runs is the arguable
  one, and it interacts with the harness-agnostic goal.
- **What happens to a user's existing herdr config.** Somebody who set
  `default_shell` for their own terminal will have it stop applying to
  Muster's panes, which is the point, and it is still a behaviour change
  worth naming in a release note rather than letting people find.
title: ⚙️ Settings a user should never leave Muster to change
